reason: Value/transfer lens: E[public] ~ +0.0003, far below the +0.002 bar. (1) The harvest has effectively already run and found nothing. The browser pass of 25 Sep 11:03-11:10 UTC (Kaggle CLI + Code tab sorted by score and by date, research/wf_ideas_v3/browser_intel.md s.2) found no public notebook above 0.953. The only notebooks >= 0.950 are x138 itself and a verbatim re-upload (kunaldesale2408). Both public post-x138 attempts failed: amanatar's x138 plus an in-sample PP sweep has an ERRORED current version and a last good run of 0.910, and seyitkaangunes' knob set scored 0.946. (2) The ceiling is overstated. The '+0.009 = 0.959-0.950+0.953-0.953' is measured against our old 0.950 base and double counts the x138 step, which #34 (x138 verbatim) already buys us. Measured against the x138 base the hard ceiling is 0.959-0.953 = +0.006. Tennant is still at 0.959 (rank 45, 40 subs, last sub 24 Sep 23:55; browser_intel.md s.1), and that is a max over ~40 public submissions on ONE embryo. The near-copy winner's curse is ~0.0013 (wf_ideas_v2/FINAL_REPORT.md l.72), so his true lever is ~+0.004-0.005 at most, and it is untested on the head (the head was not public until 24 Sep). (3) The incentives argue against a release. The LB has 3,899 teams, with 401 at >= 0.953 and 240 tied at exactly 0.953. Silver (top 5%, ~rank 195) falls INSIDE the 0.953 tie block, so every team at 0.954-0.959 (~122, Tennant and Pothula included) holds its medal only because the copy mass cannot reach it. A release of >= 0.955 would push hundreds of copiers level with its author. Both authors have so far published only ~0.003-0.013 below their own scores. P(a >= 0.955 public release by 28 Sep) ~0.15-0.25 (guess), not 0.3. (4) Conditional value and transfer. The most likely release is x138 plus public-LB-swept knobs from one of the 0.954-0.956 teams: +0.001-0.003 public, 5 subs/day selected on the public embryo, and ~0 or negative on private (71%, unseen embryos). Public-selected post-processing transferred at <= 0.5x before: division insertion lab +0.0019 -> LB +0.001; filters lab +0.01 -> LB 0 (BRIEF s.1). A single 0.954-0.955 score is inside LB noise (0.003; byte-identical 0.946/0.942, discussions_summary.md l.101,128) and within +0.001 of our expected F1 (x138 +/- divinsert, 0.953-0.954). Only a genuine new mechanism (a second head, a relink stage) of >= 0.956 would transfer. Estimate: P ~0.2 x P(mechanism, not knobs) ~0.5 x ~+0.002 true gain over F1, plus the knob branch at ~+0.0005, gives E[public] ~ +0.0003 and E[private] ~ +0.0001..+0.0002. (5) One number in the idea is too pessimistic, but it does not help: 240/240 copies land exactly at 0.953, so x138-type notebooks are deterministic and a verbatim fork reproduces with P ~0.9, not 0.6. The binding factor is whether anything exists at all, and as of today nothing does. The idea ignores the 0.99 target; its best case is 0.959. Agree with the sibling verdicts v_github-intel_successor-port_{value,schedule}.json (same idea, both refuted).
